claim: Exploratory modeling experiments that instantiate idealized aspects of a theory can help build intuition for the theory, lead to predictions, and inspire new experiments, as exemplified by the Hopfield model revealing properties later identified experimentally.
falsifier: One can test this by conducting exploratory modeling experiments based on a theory and assessing whether they generate novel predictions that are later confirmed experimentally.

conditions: When models are used to explore idealized aspects of a theory
exclusions: Limited to the reviewed example of the Hopfield model and similar exploratory modeling in theoretical neuroscience; transferability to other fields is unestablished.
